question.problem:
Find the coordinates of $A$ which is the point of intersection of the curve $y=\frac{6}{x-2}$ and the line $y=-4.$

The coordinates of $A$ are $($
{{field-1}},
{{field-2}}$)$
question.worked_solution:
We need to solve the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}y=\frac{6}{x-2} \\ y=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the equations equal to one another and solving, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{x-2} & =-4 \\ 6 & =-4x+8 \\ -2 & =-4x \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the $x$-coordinate of the intersection point is $x=\frac{1}{2}.$ Since the line is $y=-4,$ the $y$-coordinate of the intersection point is $-4.$

Therefore, the point of intersection is $A=(\,\frac{1}{2},-4).$
